The '''1960–61 Turkish National League''' was the third season of professional [[Association football|football]] in [[Turkey]]. The league consisted of 20 clubs, with [[Fenerbahçe S.K.|Fenerbahçe]] winning their second title.<ref name=rsssf>{{cite web | url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablest/turkhist.html | title=Turkey - Final Tables | website=[[RSSSF]] | access-date=15 October 2010}}</ref><ref name=turkishsoccer>{{cite web | url=https://www.angelfire.com/nj/sivritepe/6061/tl.html | title=1960-1961 Milli Lig | author=Sivritepe, Erdinç | publisher=turkish-soccer.com | access-date=15 October 2010}}</ref><ref name=tff>{{cite web | url=http://www.tff.org/default.aspx?pageID=379 | title=SPOR TOTO SÜPER LİG ŞAMPİYONLUKLARI | publisher=tff.org | language=tr | access-date=15 October 2010}}</ref>

==Overview==
[[Fenerbahçe S.K.|Fenerbahçe]] won their second Milli Lig title after edging out rivals [[Galatasaray S.K. (football team)|Galatasaray]] by one point. The previous years champion, [[Beşiktaş J.K.|Beşiktaş]], finished in third. Fenerbahçe were the lone Turkish representatives at the [[1961–62 European Cup]], as Turkey did not send a team to the [[Inter-Cities Fairs Cup]], and there was no cup competition held to send winners to the [[European Cup Winners' Cup]]. [[Metin Oktay]] finished top scorer for the third time in a row, scoring 36 goals, his highest tally to date.<ref name=rsssf /><ref name=turkishsoccer /><ref name=tff />

The season marked the first time a club from outside of [[Ankara]], [[Istanbul]] or [[İzmir]] competed; [[Adana Demirspor]] earned promotion to the league the previous season. Their stay did not last long, as they were relegated back to the Adana Regional League after finishing bottom of the table and finishing 4th in the Baraj Games. Adana Demirspor were the only club to be relegated and [[Yeşildirek SK|Yeşildirek]] were the only club to be promoted.<ref name=rsssf /><ref name=turkishsoccer /><ref name=tff />
